description: Create Mongoose models and update database configuration, then rewrite all three services (authService, issuesService, commentsService) to use MongoDB via Mongoose instead of in-memory arrays.
steps: Update server/src/config/database.js to use the connection URI: mongodb+srv://ibrarmanihar02_db_user:bymyb57CfRyzJrYp@cluster0.dbqpxjd.mongodb.net/?appName=Cluster0

Create server/src/models/User.js with Mongoose schema matching current user fields: name (String, required), email (String, required, unique), password (String, required), city (String, required), profilePictureUrl (String, default placeholder), totalPosts (Number, default 0), totalUpvotes (Number, default 0), timestamps: true. Add a virtual 'id' getter that returns _id.toString() and configure toJSON/toObject to include virtuals and map _id to id.

Create server/src/models/Issue.js with Mongoose schema matching current issue fields: title (String, required), description (String, required), category (String, required), city (String, required), location (String, required), imageUrl (String, default placeholder), reporterId (String, required), status (String, default 'open'), upvoteCount (Number, default 0), upvoters ([String], default []), timestamps: true. Same virtual id approach.

Create server/src/models/Comment.js with Mongoose schema matching current comment fields: issueId (String, required), userId (String, required), text (String, required), timestamps: true. Same virtual id approach.

Rewrite server/src/services/authService.js to use the User model. Replace all users.find/push/filter calls with User.findOne, User.create, User.find, User.findByIdAndUpdate. Keep the same public method signatures and return shapes. The generateToken and verifyToken methods use the user's MongoDB _id (as string) for the JWT payload 'id' field. The sanitizeUser method should use .toObject() and remove password.

Rewrite server/src/services/issuesService.js to use the Issue model. Replace in-memory array operations with Issue.find (with MongoDB query filters for city/category/status and $regex for search), Issue.findById, Issue.create, Issue.findByIdAndUpdate, Issue.findByIdAndDelete. Keep same method signatures. For sorting, use Mongoose .sort(). For upvote toggle logic, use $addToSet/$pull or check the upvoters array. Return objects should include 'id' field (mapped from _id).

Rewrite server/src/services/commentsService.js to use the Comment model. Replace in-memory array operations with Comment.find({issueId}), Comment.findById, Comment.create, Comment.findByIdAndUpdate, Comment.findByIdAndDelete. Keep same method signatures.
Update server/src/middleware/auth.js - the decoded JWT token will have 'id' as the user's MongoDB _id string. Ensure req.user.id works correctly with the new service methods that use findById.
Delete server/src/models/placeholder.js since it is no longer needed.

Make all controller methods properly await the now-async service methods. Currently some controller methods in issuesController.js and commentsController.js call service methods synchronously (e.g., issuesService.getAllIssues). After the migration these will all return promises, so ensure every service call is awaited.
acceptance_criteria: Server starts and logs 'Connected to MongoDB' without errors
All three Mongoose models (User, Issue, Comment) are properly defined with schemas matching the existing data shapes
API response shapes remain identical: issues have id, title, description, category, city, location, imageUrl, reporterId, status, upvoteCount, upvoters, createdAt, updatedAt
Users have id, name, email, city, profilePictureUrl, createdAt, totalPosts, totalUpvotes (password excluded)
Comments have id, issueId, userId, text, createdAt, updatedAt
Auth flow works: register creates user in MongoDB, login finds user and validates password, JWT contains user's MongoDB _id as 'id'
verification: Run 'cd /projects/sandbox/CivicWorld/server && timeout 15 node index.js' and confirm the output contains 'Connected to MongoDB' and the server starts on port 5000
